source.title: Sapiens2
source.authors: Rawal Khirodkar; He Wen; Julieta Martinez; Yuan Dong; Zhao-En Su; Shunsuke Saito

record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream performance across model sizes in human-centric vision, a setting outside language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The study reports downstream task metrics across Sapiens2 sizes and explicitly describes predictable gains with increased scale. It does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy, fit power laws, test extrapolation from small runs, or compare compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Architecture and resolution comparisons are not rows for the tested version unless they also compare scale.
record.test_reason: This is a release paper for a family of human-centric vision transformers. It reports downstream metrics for four model sizes (0.4B to 5B) and remarks, citing Kaplan, on 'predictable gains with increased scale'. It reports no pretraining loss, fits no power law, makes no extrapolation, varies no compute allocation and does not measure predictability. The size sweep is also confounded: the 0.4B, 0.8B and 1B models are revisions of different first-generation parents, the 5B model is new, and depth and width change together. V1 to V4 and V7 concern language-model loss. V5 requires the power-law form, which is never fitted here. V6 concerns the language models the claim is about. The finding, monotone downstream gains with size in vision, is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The scaling remark appears only in the pose paragraph of Sec. 6.3 ('consistent with scaling laws Kaplan et al.'), and albedo is said to improve consistently with scale. The conclusion itself makes no scaling claim: it presents Sapiens2 as outperforming general-purpose models on human-centric dense tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Vision-model scaling and downstream evaluation rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Dense-probing trends are not strictly monotonic for segmentation mIoU and normal-estimation MAE. The study also reports 1B-4K variants for some tasks, but those are resolution comparisons rather than model-size comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: Across four Sapiens2 sizes (0.4B-5B), fine-tuned metrics improve almost monotonically with size: pose mAP 76.9→82.3, segmentation mIoU 79.5→82.5, normal MAE 8.63→6.73°, albedo MAE 0.0183→0.0119. Dense probing is non-monotone at 1B for segmentation and normals. The sweep is confounded with architecture changes, and no fit is made.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream dense-prediction performance of self-supervised vision transformers improves with parameter count (qualitative, unfitted).

record.problems: The study reports only a small set of vision-model sizes and downstream task metrics; it does not fit or validate a power-law prediction, measure held-out pretraining loss, or vary compute allocations. Uncertainty estimates are not reported for the scaling results.
record.rows_left_out: Other metrics reported alongside the selected primary metric for each task were not added, as the instructions call for additional metric rows when they disagree with the primary metric or are explicitly compared. The 1B-4K entries in Tables 4 and 6 were left out because they vary resolution, not model size.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss and no power law in parameters, data or compute.
No fits on small runs and no extrapolation to larger runs.
Vision setting, but no power-law form is fitted to loss or metrics.
No language-model downstream evaluation and no test of whether gains are predictable from scale or loss.
No fitting choices, exponents or curvature examined.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are dropped. The rows are vision-model downstream metrics with no predictability test, so they do not bear on V6 as scoped to language models, and not on V5 because no power-law form is fitted. No uncertainty is reported. The sizes differ in depth, width and parent model.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation as a function of compute.
Controlled comparison of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The study uses vision models, but does not test whether power-law loss scaling holds in another modality or training regime.
Does not relate downstream performance to pretraining loss or make quantitative out-of-range predictions.
Does not compare fitting choices, fitted exponents, or compute-optimal splits, or test departures from a power law.

rows.subject: Sapiens2-0.4B
rows.stage_stated: frozen pretrained backbone; task-specific dense-probe decoder trained
rows.operation_detail: Dense-probing result in the Sapiens2 model-size sweep.
rows.note: One of four model sizes reported for this task.
rows.check: Frozen-backbone dense probing of vision models (Table 2): downstream metrics, not LM loss, with no power-law fit. The parenthesised deltas on the 5B rows (e.g. +6.5, -0.36) are gains over the best baseline, not over the next size. r7 (segmentation mIoU 65.2 vs 66.9 at 0.8B) and r15 (normal MAE 14.5 vs 14.4) are non-monotone in size.

rows.check: Fine-tuned pointmap, normal and albedo results (Tables 5-7): monotone improvement with size in vision, but no power law, loss or predictability test. Pointmap RMSE is non-monotone (0.459 at 0.8B vs 0.478 at 1B) and was not recorded.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

Table 5, Sapiens2-5B, distance absolute error L2 (e−1)

relation.reason: Section 6.3 invokes Kaplan et al. to interpret pose gains; no scaling law is fitted, evaluated or used as a quantitative tool.

tranche.reason: The model-size sweep reports downstream vision performance, but establishes no power-law form, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation or quantitative downstream prediction. Monotone improvements and the qualitative predictability remark do not establish V6 predictability.

source_check.notes: Parenthesized deltas compare against other models, not adjacent Sapiens2 sizes: Table 2 uses the best baseline; Tables 3–4 use Sapiens-2B. Pose test size is internally inconsistent: Section 6.1 and Table 3 say 11K, whereas Appendix Table 8 says 10K.
